source.title: Some open problems in invariant theory

trace.notes: Normalized the single URL input as the zbMATH resolver record https://zbmath.org/124451. Local shell fetching failed with network_or_dns_failure for zbmath.org. Local workflow resolver rows and accessible resolver/search metadata identified the exact work as V. L. Popov and E. B. Vinberg, 'Some open problems in invariant theory', Contemporary Mathematics 131.3, pages 485-497, 1992, Zbl 0783.14028, DOI 10.1090/conm/131.3/1175902.

failure_mode=metadata_only. The zbMATH URL and exact DOI resolve to bibliographic identity information, author-profile snippets, or AMS table-of-contents/product pages. These sources confirm the work identity but do not expose the article body or any complete problem statements, so they were not used as a technical extraction source.

failure_mode=metadata_only / paywalled_or_restricted / ambiguous_resolution. Bounded exact-work recovery searched the DOI, exact title plus PDF, exact title plus Popov and Vinberg, MR 1175902, and the Contemporary Mathematics volume/page range. Inspected candidates included AMS eBook and bookstore pages, Steklov/MathNet author publication lists, OUCI citation/reference pages, a 2022 Panyushev slide deck with a similar title, Taylor & Francis and Academia pages for Jerzy Weyman's different work with the same title, and related/citing invariant-theory papers. Candidates were rejected when they were metadata-only, paywalled/product pages, search snippets, citing references, slides by a different author, or a different work.
No document map was created because no readable exact-work PDF or full HTML artifact containing the problem statements was recovered.

Source adequacy gate failed: the workflow forbids extracting questions from resolver metadata, author publication lists, tables of contents, search snippets, citations, abstracts, or related works when the technical problem statements are not visible in the chosen source.
Saved exact JSON output to outputs/parse-paper/124451.json and outputs/latest.json.
